title: Generation of the HAP1 ATG9A-GFP Cell Line
author: Daniel Bernklau
materials: Mix the solutions and incubate for 00:15:00 at Room temperature .

Subject the positive clones (correct integration, expression of tagged protein at endogenous levels, typical protein pattern in starvation assay, negative for Cas9) to further validation by gDNA isolation (Thermo Scientific Gene Jet #K0721), PCR amplification of the locus and expanded sequencing of the integration site.

steps.title: Design repair template plasmid
steps.instruction: Assemble a pUC‑19‑based repair template containing ~1400 bp upstream genomic DNA of the ATG9A stop codon, monomeric EGFP CDS, a 3C cleavage site, a FLAG tag, and ~1500 bp downstream genomic DNA (including the stop codon); insert linkers (Addgene 244942) and silently mutate any PAM sites in exons.

steps.title: Clone guide RNAs into AIO‑Puro
steps.instruction: Select two guide RNAs near the ATG9A stop codon using CRISPick and clone them into the AIO‑Puro vector (Addgene 74119) following the vector’s instructions.

steps.title: Culture HAP1 wild‑type cells
steps.instruction: Grow HAP1 wild‑type cells in 10 cm culture dishes (Eppendorf #0030702115) until they reach approximately 70 % confluence.

steps.title: Refresh medium before transfection
steps.instruction: Replace the growth medium with fresh IMDM supplemented with penicillin/streptomycin and 10 % fetal calf serum 30 minutes prior to transfection.

steps.title: Prepare FuGENE‑6 transfection mix
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL FuGENE 6 transfection reagent (Promega, Cat# E2691) to 500 µL OptiMEM (Gibco 11058021).

steps.title: Add DNA to transfection mix
steps.instruction: To the same 500 µL OptiMEM, add 5 µg AIO‑Puro plasmid containing the guide RNAs and 5 µg of the homology‑template plasmid.

steps.title: Incubate transfection mixture
steps.instruction: Incubate the combined mixture at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add mixture to cells
steps.instruction: Add the transfection mixture dropwise to the cells.

steps.title: Set up non‑transfected control
steps.instruction: Prepare a parallel culture of cells that receives no transfection reagents to serve as a non‑transfected control.

steps.title: Add puromycin 24 h post‑transfection
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after transfection, replace the medium with IMDM + P/S + 10 % FCS containing 5 µg/mL puromycin.

steps.title: Apply puromycin selection
steps.instruction: Maintain puromycin selection for 48 hours or until the non‑transfected control cells are dead.

steps.title: Bulk sort GFP‑positive cells
steps.instruction: Enrich GFP‑positive cells by bulk fluorescence‑activated cell sorting (FACS).

steps.title: Expand bulk‑sorted cells
steps.instruction: Plate the bulk‑sorted GFP‑positive cells in a 10 cm dish and expand them until confluent.

steps.title: Single‑cell sort into 96‑well plates
steps.instruction: Perform a FACS single‑cell sort of the expanded cells into individual wells of 96‑well plates.

steps.title: Expand clones and PCR screen
steps.instruction: Grow the single‑cell clones to sufficient density and test each for correct integration of the homology arms by PCR.

steps.title: Prepare crude gDNA from clones
steps.instruction: Generate crude genomic DNA from each 96‑well clone for PCR screening.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium and wash the well once with DPBS.
Add 20 µL Trypsin and incubate at 37 °C for ~3 minutes.
Neutralize trypsin by adding 100 µL medium and pipette thoroughly.
Transfer the cell suspension to a PCR plate; cover with foil.
Centrifuge the plate for 2 minutes in a plate centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant carefully and wash once with PBS.
Add 25 µL Milli‑Q water to the well.
Place the plate on ice and add 5 µL proteinase K (2 mg/mL in Milli‑Q, Sigma‑Aldrich P6556).
Inactivate proteinase K by heating at 95 °C for 10 seconds.
Use 2.5 µL of this crude gDNA as template in a 12 µL PCR reaction.

steps.title: Perform PCR for integration
steps.instruction: Run PCR with the crude gDNA template to verify correct locus integration.

steps.title: Assess ATG9‑GFP protein by western blot
steps.instruction: Compare the size and expression level of ATG9‑GFP in edited clones to wild‑type cells using western blot analysis.

steps.title: Starvation assay for autophagy markers
steps.instruction: Subject PCR‑positive clones that passed quality control to a starvation assay and evaluate autophagy markers.

substeps.instruction: Wash the cells with PBS (first wash).
Wash the cells with PBS again (second wash).

steps.title: Test for Cas9 integration by western blot
steps.instruction: Analyze the clones for unintended Cas9 integration into the genome by western blotting.
